Assert that every key occurs in a reference register

Source: R/ensure_matched.R
ensure_matched.Rd

Reports rows of data whose key does not occur in reference. Duplicate reference keys do not multiply rows; use ensure_unique() separately if the reference must also be unique. Only the direction from data to reference is checked. Missing key components never match by default.

Usage

ensure_matched(
  data,
  reference,
  by,
  na_matches = c("never", "na"),
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, a database table (dbplyr, e.g. DuckDB) or an Arrow table or dataset; see Database and Arrow tables.

reference

A reference data frame or database/Arrow table. For database input, a local reference is sent as an inline query; remote references must be on the same connection. Local input requires a local reference. No table is written to the database.

by

Character vector of key columns, optionally named to map names in data to names in reference, e.g. c(cpr = "person_id"). Required: no implicit natural join is performed.

na_matches

"never" (default), or "na" to match missing keys.

success_msg

Message shown when the rule holds. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the console names every check that ran, and a description of the check otherwise.

warn_msg

Message when unmatched rows are found.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when the rule is broken. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

Value

data invisibly, unchanged. Failures carry unmatched input rows.

See also

ensure_unique(), checkpoints.

Examples

income <- data.frame(cpr = c("a", "b"), year = 2024)
population <- data.frame(cpr = "a", year = 2024)
ensure_matched(income, population, by = c("cpr", "year"))
#> Warning: Keys missing from the reference: cpr, year
#> ℹ 1 row found:
#>     cpr    year
#>     <chr> <dbl>
#>   1 b      2024
